title: Sixth Street product principles

settled.principle: Solve a concrete recurring Zenless Zone Zero player decision faster and more clearly than a generic encyclopedia page.
Lead with the decision-bearing matchup, operation, or next action; provenance and raw detail support that decision instead of dominating it.
evidence: GPT Pro DA product review recorded in Sixthstreet Prep

settled.principle: Preserve source strength, provenance, freshness, cohort, and uncertainty; fail closed instead of converting observation into recommendation or unsupported mechanics.
Use actual ZZZ and New Eridu vocabulary plus plain player actions; let utility and a coherent visual system carry the worldbuilding.
A player can complete the same core decision at 360px; only secondary detail may progressively disclose.
Use a dense, tactile, non-SaaS information system whose color and hierarchy encode stable meaning; mode differences reflect actual rules rather than decoration.
evidence: AI Project Runway: Sixthstreet Prep information architecture and DA review rows

settled.principle: Prove one bounded decision job before adding account import, OCR, generalized planning, or persistent-profile infrastructure.
evidence: AI Project Runway: Sixthstreet Prep first wedge and import/OCR rows

provisionalOrLocal: An operations-briefing metaphor may fit a particular accepted surface, but it is not a universal Sixth Street product law.
Random Play may be a visual or memory anchor without becoming the literal narrator of every product surface.
Exact hero compositions, headlines, labels, and palette choices remain local product decisions unless separately converged.
rejectedCalibration: Generic cyberpunk, SaaS-dashboard, glassmorphism, or empty marketing-page treatments.
Invented game-like verbs or mechanics used only for flavor, including describing Deadly Assault or Shiyu Defense as queueing.
Usage or observed-clear data presented as a recommendation without evidence that supports recommendation authority.
